reference.title: Urothelial carcinoma subtypes & divergent differentiation (WHO 5th)
reference.intro: WHO 5th edition (2022) recommends reporting any aggressive urothelial subtype (micropapillary, plasmacytoid, nested, sarcomatoid) and divergent differentiation (squamous, glandular) with an estimated percentage.
reference.note: Photomicrographs are from Wikimedia Commons under open Creative Commons licences. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Non-invasive papillary & conventional invasive urothelial carcinoma
points: Non-invasive papillary UC (pTa): branching fibrovascular papillae lined by urothelium with orderly (low-grade) or disordered pleomorphic (high-grade) architecture and an intact basement membrane.
Conventional invasive UC: irregular nests, cords and sheets of malignant urothelial cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and desmoplastic stroma; GATA3+, p63+, uroplakin II/III+, CK7+, CK20 variable.

images.caption: Low-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma: ordered papillary fronds with mild nuclear variation and preserved polarity.

groups.heading: Micropapillary urothelial carcinoma
points: Small tight clusters and slender tufts lacking true fibrovascular cores within prominent lacunar retraction spaces ('reverse polarity').
High rate of lymphovascular invasion and nodal metastasis; report percentage even when focal.

images.caption: Micropapillary urothelial carcinoma: tight small clusters and tufts within lacunar retraction spaces.

groups.heading: Plasmacytoid urothelial carcinoma
points: Discohesive sheets and single-file cords of cells with eccentric nuclei and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm (resembling plasma cells or lobular breast / signet-ring carcinoma).
Characterised by CDH1 (E-cadherin) loss, GATA3+, CD138+ (pitfall: do not misdiagnose as plasmacytoma!); high risk of occult peritoneal and radial margin spread.

images.caption: Plasmacytoid urothelial carcinoma: discohesive cells with eccentric nuclei and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm.

groups.heading: Nested urothelial carcinoma
points: Deceptively bland, closely packed nests and tubules infiltrating deeply into the lamina propria and muscularis propria.
Distinguish from von Brunn nests and florid cystitis cystica by deep irregular infiltration into muscularis propria, focal deeper nuclear atypia, and TERT promoter mutation.

images.caption: Nested urothelial carcinoma: deceptively bland infiltrative urothelial nests simulating von Brunn nests.

groups.heading: Sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma
points: Biphasic tumour showing both malignant epithelial (usually high-grade UC or CIS) and malignant spindle cell / pleomorphic mesenchymal-like components (may contain heterologous osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma or rhabdomyosarcoma).
Distinguish from postoperative spindle cell nodule and inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour (check ALK, marked pleomorphism, atypical mitoses, GATA3/p63/keratin).

images.caption: Sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma: pleomorphic malignant spindle cell proliferation with high mitotic activity.

groups.heading: Clear cell (glycogen-rich) UC & divergent differentiation
points: Clear cell (glycogen-rich) UC: high-grade UC with abundant clear cytoplasm (GATA3+, PAX8-negative); distinguish from Mullerian clear cell adenocarcinoma (PAX8+, HNF1B+, tubulocystic/hobnail) and metastatic clear cell RCC (PAX8+, CAIX+).

Squamous or glandular differentiation: report as urothelial carcinoma with squamous/glandular differentiation (and estimate %) rather than pure SCC or adenocarcinoma whenever any urothelial component or UCIS is present.

images.caption: Clear cell (glycogen-rich) urothelial carcinoma: sheets of high-grade urothelial cells with optically clear cytoplasm.

reference.title: WHO 5th grading of urothelial & non-urothelial bladder carcinomas
reference.intro: Urothelial carcinomas use the two-tier WHO/ISUP system (Low-grade vs High-grade); virtually all invasive urothelial carcinomas and all subtypes (micropapillary, plasmacytoid, nested, sarcomatoid) are High-grade.
reference.note: Photomicrographs are from Wikimedia Commons under open Creative Commons licences. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Low-grade vs High-grade urothelial carcinoma
points: Low-grade papillary UC: overall orderly appearance with mild variation in nuclear size, shape and chromatin, rare basally located mitoses.
High-grade UC: architectural disorder, marked nuclear pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, prominent nucleoli, and frequent mitoses including upper layers and atypical forms.

images.caption: Low-grade papillary urothelial carcinoma: cohesive fronds with minimal pleomorphism and preserved polarity.

groups.heading: Non-urothelial bladder carcinomas
points: Pure squamous cell carcinoma and pure adenocarcinoma are graded G1 (well), G2 (moderately), or G3 (poorly differentiated).
Small cell and large cell neuroendocrine carcinomas are high-grade by definition.

reference.title: Urothelial carcinoma in situ (UCIS) vs benign / reactive urothelium
reference.intro: Flat UCIS shows full-thickness or pagetoid severe cytologic atypia and frequently denudes ('clinging CIS'). Use CK20, p53 and CD44 as an adjunct panel only when H&E is equivocal.
reference.note: Photomicrographs are from Wikimedia Commons under open Creative Commons licences. ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Urothelial carcinoma in situ (H&E, CK20, p53)
points: H&E: large pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei (>= 5x lymphocyte size), loss of polarity, frequent mitoses and discohesive / clinging cells.
IHC triad for UCIS: full-thickness aberrant CK20 positivity, aberrant p53 (diffuse strong nuclear overexpression OR complete null loss), and loss of basal CD44.

images.caption: Urothelial carcinoma in situ (H&E): marked nuclear enlargement, hyperchromasia, pleomorphism and loss of polarity.
UCIS — CK20 IHC: strong full-thickness cytoplasmic positivity (contrast with umbrella-cell-only staining in benign urothelium).
UCIS — p53 IHC: diffuse strong nuclear overexpression (aberrant mutant-type staining).

groups.heading: Benign & reactive urothelium (mimics)
points: Benign urothelium preserves maturation towards large superficial umbrella cells (which may be binucleated or mildly enlarged) with regular nuclear membranes and open chromatin.

Reactive atypia (inflammation, catheter, BCG, radiation): uniform vesicular nuclei with prominent single nucleoli, preserved polarity, umbrella-only CK20, wild-type patchy p53, and full-thickness CD44.

images.caption: Benign urothelium: preserved polarity with prominent superficial umbrella cells (avoid mistaking large umbrella nuclei for CIS).

options: Perivesical soft tissue, macroscopic extravesical mass (pT3b)

reference.title: Urinary bladder staging landmarks (pT1–pT4b)
reference.intro: Distinguish thin discontinuous muscularis mucosae (pT1) from thick compact muscularis propria bundles (pT2), and distinguish direct transmural prostatic stroma invasion (pT4a) from urethral/ductal spread (staged separately).
reference.note: ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Lamina propria (pT1) vs muscularis propria (pT2a / pT2b)
points: pT1: invasion into lamina propria, including around or into thin wispy fascicles of muscularis mucosae (often accompanied by large blood vessels).
pT2a vs pT2b: thick, compact smooth muscle bundles of detrusor (muscularis propria); inner half = pT2a, outer half = pT2b.

links.label: ExpertPath: Staging of Urinary Bladder Carcinoma

groups.heading: Perivesical soft tissue (pT3a vs pT3b)
points: Fat is normally present within the muscularis propria — do NOT call pT3 unless tumour extends BEYOND the outer contour of the muscularis propria into true perivesical adipose tissue.
pT3a: microscopic extension into perivesical fat; pT3b: grossly visible extravesical mass / nodule.

links.label: ExpertPath: Staging of Urinary Bladder Carcinoma

groups.heading: Prostatic stroma invasion (pT4a pitfall)
points: Direct transmural invasion through the bladder wall into prostatic stroma = pT4a.

Subepithelial invasion into prostatic stroma arising from urothelial carcinoma/CIS of the prostatic urethra or prostatic ducts/acini is NOT bladder pT4a (it is staged under the urethra protocol, pT2).

links.label: ExpertPath: Staging of Urinary Bladder Carcinoma

groups.heading: Adjacent pelvic organs (pT4a) vs pelvic/abdominal wall (pT4b)
points: pT4a: direct extravesical invasion into seminal vesicles, uterus, vagina, or prostatic stroma (transmural).
pT4b: direct invasion into the pelvic wall or abdominal wall.

links.label: ExpertPath: Staging of Urinary Bladder Carcinoma

reference.title: Cystectomy surgical margins (ureteral, urethral, soft tissue)
reference.intro: Report ureteral, urethral and perivesical soft tissue margins separately for both invasive carcinoma and urothelial carcinoma in situ (CAP 4.2.0.0).
reference.note: ExpertPath pages open with your own ExpertPath login; the app holds none of their images.

groups.heading: Ureteral and urethral mucosal margins
points: Submit en-face rings of right ureter, left ureter and distal urethral/apical margin (or final shaved intraoperative frozen-section margins if revised).
Clearly distinguish involvement by invasive carcinoma from flat UCIS or low-grade dysplasia.

links.label: ExpertPath: Cystectomy Specimen Handling and Margins

groups.heading: Perivesical soft tissue (radial) margins
points: Ink the entire non-peritonealised perivesical soft tissue surface before opening the bladder.
Tumour on ink = positive soft tissue margin; if negative, record distance in mm to the closest inked soft tissue surface.
